localChanges: Computer players now choose what to build by how long it will take: a city only starts a unit, an improvement, a ship or a Wonder it can finish in reasonable time at the shields it has left after supporting its units, and picks units for their strength per shield rather than the strongest it knows. They finish many more improvements as a result, and start fewer Wonders (#212).

Martial law now works as it does in Civ1: up to three units in a city each keep one unhappy citizen content, only units that can attack count, and it applies after Temples, Colosseums and Cathedrals have done their part (#224).
Entertainers now come out of a city's content citizens before its unhappy ones, as in Civ1, so a large city's unrest can always be calmed by taking enough citizens off the land (#224).

log: Checked against OpenCivOne's decompile of the city happiness routine (`src/Game/CodeObjects/CityWorker.cs`, L1444-1575), martial law differed in three ways (civ-clone/web-renderer#224):
The cap is 3 units (`if (attackUnitCount > 3) attackUnitCount = 3`), not 4.

A unit counts if its type's attack strength isn't 0, not if it's `Fortifiable`: Diplomats no longer count, ships and aircraft do. Only the city owner's units count, as the original walks that player's units on the city's square.

It applies after the Colosseum, Cathedral and Temple (and the Oracle and Michelangelo's), so it calms what they leave. The rule now has `Priority(3500)`, after every `Low` improvement and Wonder rule here and in civ1-wonder, and before Shakespeare's Theatre (4000). The net unhappiness is the same either way; what changes is how many units the `MartialLaw` yields say are in use, which the city screen and the computer players read.

The governments are unchanged. `martialLaw.ts` exports them (`martialLawGovernments`), the cap (`martialLawUnitLimit`) and the unit test (`keepsMartialLaw`) so consumers don't repeat them. The rule has an id, `civ1-city-happiness:city/cost/martial-law`.
Not modelled: the original also counts the two `FirstFortifiedCityUnits` slots in the city record, which the engine has no equivalent of.

Tests: the governments and cap; 3 of 4 Warriors used; no more units than unhappy citizens; a Trireme counts, Settlers and a Diplomat don't; none under a Republic; with a Temple (2 with Mysticism) and 3 Warriors against 4 unhappy, the Temple calms 2 and martial law the other 2. The existing martial-law tests in `yield.test.ts` use Warriors with civ1-unit's yields, and the cap is now 3.
civ-clone/web-renderer#224 asked whether Entertainers can calm a size-8 city with 3 unhappy citizens. In v474.05 they can (3 of them), and here they couldn't with any number.

v474.05 (OpenCivOne's decompile, `CityWorker.cs`: the happiness routine and `F0_1d12_6dfe_AdjustHappyUnhappyCitizens`, whose `size` argument is the specialist count) clamps happy + unhappy to the working citizens right after setting the base unhappiness, while nobody is happy yet: so specialists come out of the content citizens, then the unhappy ones. Luxuries come after, and each excess happy face cancels an unhappy one (`H--, U--`), so a point of luxury makes a content citizen happy or, with none left, an unhappy one content.

`calculateCitizenState` followed Rome on 640K a Day (p249): it applied Happiness first and then took specialists from the content citizens, then the happy ones, then the unhappy. Once the content citizens ran out each Entertainer's own luxury made a happy citizen that the next specialist removed, so they never calmed a city.

It now takes specialists out first (content, then unhappy), then applies Happiness. Its loop also no longer spends a point it doesn't have: with one point left at an unhappy citizen it made them content and then happy as well.
Size 8, 3 unhappy, k Entertainers (k Happiness): k = 3 gives 2 happy and 2 unhappy, calm, as in v474.05 (H 3 + U 3 > 5 working: H 2, U 2); k = 2 stays in disorder in both.

Not changed, and still different from v474.05: the engine nets every Unhappiness yield before assigning moods, where the original applies luxuries, then improvements, then martial law, then Wonders, clamping in between. Totals of happy minus unhappy mostly agree; the split between them can differ.

Tests: the specialist order and the single spend in `calculateCitizenState`; disorder with 2 and 3 Entertainers in a size-8 city with 3 unhappy; the old "specialists take the happy citizens" disorder case is now calm.
chore: CI compiles and fails on stale compiled output, as core-strategy's does (civ-clone/web-renderer#66)
core-terrain-feature and simple-world-generator are imported by nothing here; civ1-city and core-science were listed in both dependencies and dev dependencies (civ-clone/web-renderer#66).

`lib/Civ1/martialLaw.ts` repeated civ1-city-happiness's martial law, 4 units under Anarchy, Communism, Despotism or Monarchy, because the rule kept them in its own closure. civ1-city-happiness now applies v474.05's (civ-clone/web-renderer#224: 3 units that can attack, after the city's improvements and Wonders) and exports `martialLawGovernments` and `martialLawUnitLimit`; the policy imports them.

Which units martial law uses is still read from the engine's `MartialLaw` yields (`martialLawUnitsIn`), so the AI counts the units the engine counts: no Diplomats, but a ship in the city. A comment in `City/defence` no longer says martial law comes first.

Tests (over the new civ1-city-happiness): a size-10 city wants 3 units, not 4; with a Temple martial law only uses two of three Warriors; a Diplomat doesn't count, so a city with two Warriors and a Diplomat builds a third unit.
Needs civ1-city-happiness's fix/martial-law-fidelity merged (the import doesn't exist before it) before CI can pass.
`getOffensiveUnit`/`getDefensiveUnit` took the unit with the most Attack/Defence whatever it cost, so a size-1 city making 1 shield could start a 40-shield Catapult (civ-clone/web-renderer#212).

`lib/City/buildTime` (generic) works out turns to finish a build item at the city's net shields (Production yields after unit support), counting the shields stored: 0 if already paid for, Infinity at 0 net shields.

`chooseUnit` replaces `getUnitByYield`: of the units the city can finish within `ProductionPolicy.buildTurns.unit` (10), the most strength per shield, then the most strength, then the cheapest. Units with no strength are ignored; obsolete units are never offered by the ruleset. Only a defender for the city itself falls back, when nothing is that soon, to the soonest (then cheapest); an attacker, or a defender for another undefended city, isn't started at all.

Tests: an attacker it can finish over a stronger one it can't; the stronger one once stored shields bring it within reach; a defender it can finish over a stronger one; the cheapest defender at 0 net shields. The existing attacker test gets 2 shields so it can finish Horsemen.

`SimpleAIClient#unitDestroyed` chose the emergency rebuild with `defaultProductionPolicy`, not the policy the player's `ChooseProduction` strategy uses (civ-clone/web-renderer#212). Harmless while every player has the default, wrong once #157 gives them their own.

`ChooseProduction#choose(player, city)` now does what `attempt` did, and the client asks the first `ChooseProduction` in its own strategy registry (kept as `_strategies`, as `StrategyAIClient`'s is private), so the rebuild uses the strategy's policy, knowledge and registries. With no `ChooseProduction` registered it falls back to the default policy as before.
Tests: a policy willing to wait 20 turns rebuilds a Phalanx and is asked for the player once; with no `ChooseProduction` the default policy rebuilds Warriors.

The explorer branch built the cheapest land unit that can fight whatever the city made, so a city on 0 net shields started Warriors it would never finish (civ-clone/web-renderer#212). It now only takes an explorer the city can finish within `buildTurns.unit`, and otherwise moves on to its other choices. The quota itself is unchanged (#229).
Test: a city on 0 net shields with land to explore doesn't start Warriors. The existing explorer test gets the 1 shield Warriors need.

Cities on 0 net shields started Settlers they would never finish (civ-clone/web-renderer#212). Settlers are now only chosen when the city can finish them within `ProductionPolicy.buildTurns.settlers` (20).
Tests: a size-2 city making 1 net shield (40 turns) doesn't start Settlers; one making 2 (20 turns) does.

`shouldBuildWonder` had no minimum: a city on 1 net shield started the Oracle at 4/300 (civ-clone/web-renderer#212). A Wonder is now only chosen when the city can finish it within `ProductionPolicy.buildTurns.wonder` (40) and makes at least `wonderShields` (5) net shields, however many it has stored. `shouldBuildWonder` compares net shields through `lib/City/buildTime`, which now takes the net shields when the caller has them.
Tests: no Colossus (200) at 4 net shields; none at 4 net shields with 190 stored. The existing Wonder tests get the 5 shields they now need.

The Wonder was picked at random from everything available, so a player with no ships could start the Lighthouse (civ-clone/web-renderer#212). `lib/Civ1/wonders` judges whether a Wonder does anything for the player: not if it's obsolete (civ1-wonder's `isObsolete`, which Civ1 applies as soon as anyone has the obsoleting advance), and the Lighthouse and Magellan's Expedition only for a player with a ship. Only useful Wonders are drawn from. civ1-wonder moves from dev dependencies to dependencies.
Tests: no obsolete Colossus; no Lighthouse without ships; the Lighthouse with a Trireme.

`BuildExplorerShip` took the cheapest ship whatever the city made, so a city on 0 net shields started a Frigate it would never finish (civ-clone/web-renderer#212). `explorerShipFor` now also requires the city to finish the ship within `explorerShipTurns` (20) at its net shields; its last argument overrides that.
Test: no Trireme (40 shields) at 1 net shield. The other ship tests give the coastal city 2 net shields, enough for a Trireme in 20 turns.

The last choice, a random pick of the remaining units and improvements, ignored cost, so a city could spend 80 turns on City Walls (civ-clone/web-renderer#212). It now draws only from what the city can finish within `buildTurns.unit` (10) for a unit or `buildTurns.improvement` (40) for an improvement, still with one draw per call.

When the city can finish none of them it builds the cheapest improvement worth having, rather than drawing from everything: units come last, as they'd cost support the city doesn't have, and Barracks and City Walls just before them, as they're only worth building on purpose.
Tests: at 1 net shield no draw picks City Walls (120 shields); at 0 net shields the first and last draws both build a Temple, not Warriors or Barracks.
At 150 turns over 40 games against 7d643a2, the first limits cost more than they saved (civ-clone/web-renderer#212):

Settlers within 20 turns cost cities (-0.80, t -2.9) and power (-29, t -2.4); 40 turns was still worse than no limit. Settlers are now built by any city that makes net shields, however long they take (`buildTurns.settlers` Infinity), so only a city that would never finish them is stopped.

A Wonder within 40 turns at 5 net shields stopped almost every Wonder: Wonders built -0.17 to -0.20 (t -3.5 to -4.1), score -3 to -6. Now 100 turns at 2 net shields, which still keeps a 1-shield city off a 300-shield Wonder.
`finishesWithin(turns, limit)` in `lib/City/buildTime` makes every limit check say no for a city making no net shields, even with no limit.
Tests: Settlers at 1 net shield, not at 0; no Pyramids (300) at 2 net shields, the Colossus (200) at 2; no Wonder at 1 net shield even with 190 stored.

Two earlier commits on this branch kept a city off Settlers it couldn't finish soon: first within 20 turns, then only at 0 net shields. Both cost the player in the arena (civ-clone/web-renderer#212), against 7d643a2:
20 turns, 40 games x 150 turns: cities -0.80 (t -2.9), power -29 (t -2.4).
0 net shields only, 80 x 150: score -3.1 (t -2.7), gold -56 (t -5.6); the same with no Wonder limit: score -2.7 (t -2.4).
No Settlers limit at all, otherwise the same: score -0.4, gold -17, both n.s.; advances and explored better.

A city's net shields when it chooses aren't what it makes over the next turns (it reassigns workers, and grows), and expansion is worth the wait. So Settlers are chosen as before this branch, and `buildTurns.settlers` is gone.

Once the random pick only drew what a city can finish, cities finished far more improvements (civ-clone/web-renderer#212), and Barracks and City Walls are only worth building on purpose: the fallback already put them after every other improvement. They're now left out of the random pick too (`onPurposeOnly`).
Test: at 3 net shields with Masonry, where both are within the improvement limit, no draw picks either.
test: say the Wonder test's city is within the 100-turn limit, not 40
